questions.q: Why should a fact table join to a dimension table on the surrogate key rather than the natural/business key?
options: Natural keys cannot be used in JOIN clauses in Snowflake SQL
It's what makes SCD Type 2 history possible without rewriting fact rows every time a dimension attribute changes
Surrogate keys are required by Snowflake's storage engine for all tables
Surrogate keys make VARIANT columns faster to query
questions.explain: Joining on the surrogate key lets a dimension carry multiple historical rows for the same natural key (SCD Type 2) without ever needing to update existing fact rows.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA(...) clause on a Task?
options: It converts the Task's warehouse to a larger size
It skips the Task's work entirely when the Stream has no unconsumed changes, keeping scheduled runs cheap
It grants the Task additional privileges automatically
It forces the Task to run twice as often
questions.explain: Without it, a scheduled Task would run its full MERGE every time regardless of whether anything changed; the WHEN clause lets it skip (visible as SKIPPED in TASK_HISTORY) when the Stream is empty.

questions.q: In the RBAC setup described, why does the analyst role receive no grants on the raw or staging schemas?
options: Because least privilege means each role gets only what it actually needs — an analyst has no legitimate reason to query raw landing data
Because Snowflake technically prevents granting SELECT on raw schemas
It was an oversight that should be fixed by granting full access
Because raw and staging schemas cannot have grants applied to them
questions.explain: The missing grant is deliberate — it reflects the real access boundary an analyst role should have, verified afterward with SHOW GRANTS rather than assumed.

questions.q: How should you verify that the RBAC configuration actually enforces the intended boundary, rather than just trusting the GRANT statements you wrote?
options: Check TASK_HISTORY only
Check the warehouse's credit usage
Run SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE against each role and confirm what it actually holds
Assume it's correct because the GRANT statements ran without error
questions.explain: SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE lists the privileges a role actually holds, which is the concrete way to confirm the least-privilege boundary is real.

questions.q: What confirms that the star schema is being kept current by a working Streams+Tasks pipeline rather than a one-time manual load?
options: The existence of a resource monitor on the warehouse
The presence of a VARIANT column in the fact table
The fact table having more rows than the staging table
Seeing real incremental run history in TASK_HISTORY, not just a single initial population
questions.explain: TASK_HISTORY showing genuine recurring runs (succeeded or correctly skipped) is the evidence that the pipeline is live and incremental, not a one-off manual load.
